title: SMB1 remake (frame-accurate Super Mario Bros. in NESFab, mapper 30)
description: A homebrew NES remake of Super Mario Bros. (1985) in NESFab (patched 1.8) for mapper 30, aiming at parity with the original: the same buttons from power-on give the same frames, enemy positions, score, sound and timing. All 32 levels of the first quest are built from the original ROM's own data by generator scripts, and 159 same-input replay cases against the original are the parity suite. SMB1 is Nintendo's game: the original ROM, anything built from its data and anything extracted from it never goes into git or docs; this manifest only says how to build and prove the remake on the user's machine.

source.referenceRom: roms/final/SMB1_Repro_20261011.nes (md5 2b02d0777b42d1ae01b014c310588975, the newest ROM of the project)

optionalInputs.description: the user's own copy of the original Super Mario Bros. ROM. NOT needed to build (measured: ./build.sh game gives the byte-identical ROM with SMB1_ORIG_ROM pointing nowhere: the level, music and sound data derived from it are already in the source tree). Needed only to regenerate that data and for the same-input parity suite; it is never copied into the repository or the output folder

toolchain: patched NESFab 1.8 shipped in tools/nesfab/nesfab.exe (a hand-edited compiler binary is a trap: the patches live in tools/nesfab-patches)

steps.name: build-game
steps.note: A failed build leaves the old .nes but EMPTIES build/*.mlb: never build while something reads build/ (the retrospective's rule); BrokenDev publishes copies.

reference.note: The project's own final ROM of 2026-10-11 (not regenerated by this build, which starts from the working tree).

run.note: Title screen with its attract demo; Start begins 1-1.

scenarios.why: The same play with BrokenNes' own power-on RAM fill (the FCEUX pattern 00 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF, the app default). The remake reads a variable it never initialises (chr_test_active) and so shows the placeholder digits and stalls on the World card. Recorded, not a verdict: see knownIssues.

oracle.why: Same method as vrun-nes. Both emulators start from zeroed work RAM (the project's own Mesen setting): with the FCEUX pattern the remake reads two uninitialised variables and stalls (see knownIssues), which is a project finding, not a difference between the emulators.

compat.what: The remake on other NES emulators, each with ITS OWN default power-on RAM (BrokenNes runs verify's powerOnRam zeros, the project's requirement). The uninit-ram check reads the variable the remake never initialises, so an emulator whose RAM does not power on as zeros shows the known bug directly.

scenarios.what: power-on, the title, Start, verify's play script (walk right, jump, run)

checks.what: the title runs (the NMI counter ticks)
the title looks like BrokenNes' title (structure, palette aside)
chr_test_active reads 0 (the remake never initialises it and relies on RAM powering on as zeros: knownIssues)
the World card ends and the level starts (levelcard_state back to 0)
holding Right scrolls the level (camera_x moves)
the game keeps running to the end (the NMI counter keeps ticking)
a picture is drawn at the end

knownIssues: PROJECT BUG, found by BrokenDev: the remake reads two variables it never initialises, chr_test_active ($07FC) and fire_anim_timer ($07AE), and relies on work RAM powering on as zeros (the project's own Mesen is set to AllZeros). Real hardware powers RAM on undefined, and BrokenNes (like FCEUX) fills it with 00 00 00 00 FF FF FF FF, which puts $FF in both: the digits 1, 2 and 3 are drawn with the test-pattern tiles ('WORLD' shows blocks, the title says '[]PLAYER GAME') and the World card never ends. Fix in the project: set both to 0 at boot (or clear all of RAM in the reset code). BrokenDev's verify runs with powerOnRam zeros so the rest of the game can be checked, and records play-fceux-ram as an information scenario to show the effect.

First quest: all 32 levels play start to finish and every level matches the original in same-input replays, but 'full parity' cannot be proven by testing, only approached: every new kind of replay found real differences the earlier ones could not see.
Work in progress that is not merged (pipeline/*_STATE.md in the archive): fix 084, castle 061/062, lag 013/014. Five Fire Mario levels (2-1, 3-2, 4-1, 8-2, 8-3) still lag.

Known small differences: Hammer Bro / Lakitu / Spiny-egg slot order, an enemy landing one frame later under a freeze (7-1), a pit game-over card 21 frames late in one forced fire case (8-4), the invisible 7-4 to 8-1 level-change reset order. Accepted: fireworks live in their own ticker, 2 of 10 enemy scenarios in verify.sh.
Resource limits: fixed bank 31 had 1,095 bytes free (floor about 1,100) and RAM 3 bytes free at the end of the work.

The replay suite compared game state, never pixels: five visible bugs survived weeks of 'parity' (retrospective section 10). BrokenDev's verify records pictures and audio on BrokenNes; it is not a parity proof against the original.
The NESFab compiler is a suspect for impossible results: compile non-determinism exists (the project's verify.sh rebuilds three times and requires identical output).
